# Page 16^page=16
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 16 Daily Content PDF NATIONAL AFFAIRS GoI Releases Rs 77.98 Crore for 755 Senior Citizen Welfare Projects Under AVYAY for Q2FY27 In November 2026, the Government of India (GoI) released Rs 77.98 crore in Grant-in-Aid to 755 projects under the Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC), a component of the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), for the 2nd Quarter (Q2: July-September) of Financial Year 2026-27(FY27). Exam Hints: ✓ What? GoI Releases Grant-in-Aid for 755 senior citizen welfare projects ✓ Total Amount Released: Rs 77.98 crore ✓ Released under: IPSrc component of AVYAY scheme ✓ Released for: Q2FY27 ✓ Scheme Administered by: DSJE, MoSJE ✓ Key Principles of Scheme: ‘Ageing with Dignity’ and ‘Ageing in Place’ ✓ Core Components: Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC); State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC); Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY); National Helpline (Toll-free No. 14567); and Regional Resource and Training Centres (RRTCs). About Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY): Key Reason: As per the Census 2011, India had 10.38 crore people aged 60 years and above, including 5.11 crore males and 5.27 crore females. Launched in: Launched in 2021, AVYAY, one of the flagship schemes of the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment (MoSJE), subsumed and expanded the previous National Action Plan for Senior Citizens (NAPSrC) by integrating multiple interventions for senior citizens under a unified umbrella scheme. Aim: The scheme is designed to provide functional support and promote active ageing by facilitating shelter, food, healthcare and recreational services. Key Principles: The scheme follows the principles of ‘Ageing with Dignity’ and ‘Ageing in Place’, promoting respectful and empowering care while enabling senior citizens to live safely, independently and with dignity in their homes and communities through community- based support services. Administered by: The Department of Social Justice & Empowerment (DSJE) of MoSJE, acts as the nodal agency for the scheme. Key Components: The scheme has key components which include: • IPSrC: It provides financial assistance to eligible organisations for running and maintenance of senior citizen homes or continuous care homes to improve the quality of life of the senior citizens. • State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC): Under this component, States and Union Territories (UTs) prepare and implement action plans customized to their respective requirements for senior citizen welfare, with financial support from the MoSJE for formulating and implementing these plans. States can utilize up to 20% of their allocated funds for these state-specific programs. • Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana (RVY): RVY, originally launched in 2017 as a standalone Central Sector Scheme (CSS), has been subsumed under the AVYAY, provides physical aids and assisted living devices for senior citizens Below the Poverty Line (BPL) and with a family income not exceeding Rs. 15,000 per month. As of date, the scheme has cumulatively benefitted more than

# Page 17^page=17
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 17 Daily Content PDF 10.45 lakh senior citizens covered with 5587653 Assistive Living Devices (ALDs) through camp mode and walk-in centres of the Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation of India (ALIMCO) at Pradhan Mantri Divyasha Vayoshri Kendras (PMD-VK). • National Helpline: The Elder Line Helpline (Toll-free No. 14567), is a National Helpline for Senior Citizens (NHSC) launched in 2021, to offer guidance, emotional support, and rescue services. • Regional Resource and Training Centres (RRTCs): These centres act as regional nodal agencies under AVYAY, particularly IPSrC, for training, capacity building, research, awareness and elderly welfare advocacy. Each RRTC receives Rs 19.58 lakh annually, with additional support provided to designated NGOs and institutions to strengthen outreach and service delivery. Key Initiatives Launched under AVYAY Scheme: JEEVAN App & SHATAYU Dashboard: IIn May 2026, the GoI launched the Joint Elderly Empowerment and Virtual Assistance Network (JEEVAN) app to provide welfare scheme information, emergency assistance and support services, and the Senior Holistic Care Assistance and Training for Your Utility (SHATAYU) dashboard to help senior citizens and families find trained geriatric caregivers. Seniorcare Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE): The Senior-care Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) initiative supports startups developing innovative elderly-care solutions with financial assistance of up to Rs 1 crore through equity participation, mentorship and market linkages. • The SAGE portal serves as a single-window platform for accessing verified elderly-care products and services. Other Key Initiatives: The Senior Citizen Opportunities for Productive Engagement (SCOPE) initiative promotes elderly participation and livelihood opportunities, while PM-Special (System for Provision of Eldercare in House and Assisted Living) provides free skill-based training through empanelled institutes to address the shortage of geriatric caregivers. About Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment (MoSJE): Union Minister- Virendra Kumar Khatik (Constituency- Tikamgarh, Madhya Pradesh, MP) Minister of State (MoS)- Ramdas Athawale (Rajya Sabha- Maharashtra); B.L. Verma (Rajya Sabha- Uttar Pradesh, UP) Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw Launches Semicon India 2.0 Portal; Approves 12 ECMS Projects In November 2026, Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), launched the Semicon 2.0 Web Application Portal under the second phase of the Semicon India Programme, at an event held in New Delhi, Delhi. • During the event, the Minister also announced the approval of 12 additional applications under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS), involving an estimated investment of Rs 7,503 crore. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of Semicon 2.0 Portal and Approval ECMS Applications ✓ Launched by: Union Minister Ashwini Kumar Vaishnaw, MeitY ✓ Applications Opened: Pillars 2, 3 and 4 ✓ Launched as part of: 2nd phase of the Semicon India Programme

# Page 18^page=18
Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 18 Daily Content PDF ✓ New ECMS Approvals: 12 ✓ Estimated Cost: Rs 7,503 crore About Semicon 2.o Portal: Following the launch of the new Semicon 2.0 portal, applications have now been operationalised for 03 of the programme’s 06 strategic pillars: machines and materials (Pillar 2), establishing additional semiconductor fabrication facilities (Pillar 3), and strengthening the Assembly, Testing, Marking and Packaging (ATMP) and Outsourced Semiconductor Assembly and Test (OSAT) industry (Pillar 4). 12 Additional Approvals under ECMS: Overview: In addition, he announced 12 additional approvals under the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) with an estimated investment of Rs 7,503 crore, bringing the total number of approved applications to 118 (covering 34 products across 16 states). Target Segment Products: The latest approvals will cover 10 target segment products, spanning: 4 components: Multi- layer Printed Circuit Board (PCB), relays, heat sinks and specialty ceramics; • 5 supply chain products: copper foil, anode material, cathode active material, polypropylene film and camera rim; and Capital Goods and their parts. Component-wise Manufacturers: Manufacturers for the component category are: NeST ICELR Private Limited (Multi- layer PCB); TDConnex (Chennai) Private Limited (Relays); Modern Automotives Limited (Heat Sinks); and Voltix Semicon Private Limited (Specialty Ceramics). • Manufacturers for supply-chain products: Indo Asia Copper Limited (copper foil); TACC Limited (anode material for lithium-ion cells); Vidyuta Materials Private Limited (cathode active material); Enerfolie LLP (polypropylene film) and Surface Modification Technologies Pvt. Ltd. (camera rims). • Manufacturers for capital goods and their parts: TDConnex (Chennai) Private Limited (precision moulds and tooling); Rockwell Automation India Private Limited (capital equipment); and Wipro Pari Robotics Private Limited (capital equipment used in factory automation and system integration). Coverage: The newly approved projects will span across 7 states i.e. Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh (MP), Maharashtra, Punjab, Tamil Nadu (TN) and Uttar Pradesh (UP). Potential Outcome: The new approved projects are expected to generate production worth Rs 39,045 crore and generate 7,127 direct employment opportunities. About Semicon 2.0: Background: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister (PM) Narendra Modi, had approved Semicon 2.0 with a total budget outlay of Rs 1,27,500 crore under the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM). Key Pillars: The 2nd phase of the programme is centered around six strategic pillars such as: Pillar 1 (Design of Chips); Pillar 2 (Machines and Materials); Pillar 3 (Setting up More Fabs); Pillar 4 (Strengthening the ATMP/OSAT Industry); Pillar 5 (Research & Development, R&D); and Pillar 6 (Talent Development). Key Projected Outcome: Now, with the approval of all 118 applications under ECMS, these projects are expected to attract a total investment of Rs 77,051 crore, with projected production worth Rs 5,73,146 crore and direct employment for 81,755 people.

Report Errors in the PDF - support@careerscloud.in Copyright 2014-2026 @ AffairsCloud.com 19 Daily Content PDF About Ministry of Electronic and IT (MeitY): Union Minister- Ashwini Vaishnaw (Rajya Sabha member- Odisha) Minister of State (MoS)- Jitin Prasada (Constituency- Pilibhit, Uttar Pradesh, UP) Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh Launches Organic Fisheries SOP; Soreng in Sikkim Becomes India’s First Organic Fisheries Cluster In November 2026, Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying (MoFAHD), launched the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for organic fisheries certification for the Northeastern Region during his visit to Mangan, Sikkim. • He also inaugurated projects worth Rs 3.75 crore under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY), while Soreng district, Sikkim, became India’s first notified Organic Fisheries Cluster under PMMSY. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Launch of SOP for Organic Certification of Fisheries in the Northeastern Region ✓ Who? Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh MoFAHD. ✓ Where? Mangan district, Sikkim ✓ When? 2 November 2026. ✓ Significance: Soreng, Sikkim was notified as India’s first Organic Fisheries Cluster under PMMSY ✓ Inauguration: PMMSY fisheries projects worth Rs 3.75 crore. ✓ National Clusters: 34 fisheries production and processing clusters ✓ Organic Fish Varieties: Amur carp, IMC and Trout. ✓ Farmer Support: 15 fish farmers from two fisheries cooperative societies. ✓ Financial Assistance: KCCs distributed; Five fish farmers received cheques under MMMUY Highlights of the Visit: Objective: Union Minister Rajiv Ranjan Singh visited Mangan district, Sikkim, to review fisheries development initiatives under PMMSY, as part of the Centre’s structured mechanism for periodic visits by Union Ministers to Northeastern states to review development programmes and obtain beneficiary feedback. Activities: The Minister visited a PMMSY-supported Live Fish Vending Centre, interacted with members of Fish Farmers’ Cooperative Societies to understand their operational challenges, and distributed fish feed to 15 fish farmers belonging to two fisheries cooperative societies. Organic Fisheries SOP: The SOP establishes a framework for organic fish production, certification and traceability, enhancing product credibility, consumer confidence and access to premium domestic and international markets. PMMSY Projects: The inaugurated project under PMMSY supports hatcheries, feed mills, cold storage, Biofloc and Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS) to strengthen production, processing, value addition and marketing across the fisheries value chain. Soreng Organic Fisheries Cluster: • Integration: The cluster integrates organic production, certification, processing, value addition and marketing to strengthen the fisheries value chain and improve market access. • Focus: The cluster promotes ecologically sustainable fish farming without harmful chemicals, antibiotics and pesticides, with emphasis on Amur carp, Indian Major Carps (IMC) and Trout, supporting premium market opportunities. • Clusters: The Government has notified 34 fisheries production and processing clusters nationwide, adopting a cluster-based approach integrating production, processing, value addition and marketing.

Objective: Launched for five years from Financial Year 2020–21 (FY21) to FY25 to usher in a Blue Revolution by targeting 22 million metric tons (MMT) of fish production, doubling fishers’ and fish farmers’ incomes, promoting sustainable fisheries and modernising infrastructure to reduce post-harvest losses. Outlay: The scheme has an estimated outlay of Rs 20,750 crore (FY21-FY27) and covers all States and Union Territories. About Sikkim: Chief Minister (CM) – Prem Singh Tamang (Golay) Governor – Dushyant Kumar Gautam Capital – Gangtok Zoological Park – Himalayan Zoological Park India–Myanmar Rahat Mitra Exercise Concludes in Chennai, TN In November 2026, India and Myanmar conducted the inaugural bilateral Tri-Services Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) Exercise ‘Rahat Mitra’ on 5–6 November 2026 in Chennai, Tamil Nadu (TN), to enhance interoperability, coordination and exchange of best practices in disaster response. • The exercise, coordinated by the Indian Navy (IN), brought together more than 300 personnel from the Indian Army (IA), Indian Air Force (IAF), IN and Myanmar Defence Forces under the theme “Together for Humanity, Stronger through Partnership.” Exam Hints: ✓ What? Inaugural India–Myanmar bilateral Tri-Services HADR Exercise ‘Rahat Mitra’. ✓ Participants? IA, IN, IAF and Myanmar Defence Forces. ✓ Where? Chennai, Tamil Nadu. ✓ When? 5–6 November 2026. ✓ Objective – Enhance operational interoperability, coordination and disaster-response preparedness. ✓ Scenario – TTX based on a severe cyclone. ✓ Indian Army – Demonstrated obstacle clearance, bridge-laying, rescue, dewatering and Flood Relief capabilities. ✓ Indian Navy – Showcased shipborne HADR, FRT and SAR capabilities. ✓ Indian Air Force – Demonstrated casualty evacuation using ALH. ✓ Infrastructure – INS Adyar and Communication Network Centre ✓ Key Aircraft/Ships – Chetak helicopter and INS Bitra participated ✓ Myanmar Participation – Commodore Aung Niang Win and two Myanmar officers participated Highlights of the Rahat Mitra Exercise 2026: Planning: A Table-Top Exercise (TTX) based on a severe cyclone scenario enabled both sides to discuss coordinated response mechanisms and joint disaster management protocols. Exam Hints: ✓ What? Notification of ‘The Immigration and Foreigners (Exemption) (Amendment) Order, 2026’ ✓ Notified by: MHA ✓ Purpose: Relaxation of Passport and Visa Rules for Several Categories ✓ Relaxation to: o Persecuted religious minorities: Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, and Christian o From Which Countries? Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan o Cut-off Date for Minorities: Entered India on or before December 31, 2024 ✓ Other Categories: Pakistan nationals (entered India on or before December 31, 2009), PIOs, Sri Lankan Tamil Refugees & Tibetans, among others Relaxation to Specific-Categories: Exemption for Pakistan Nationals: Those who entered India on or before 31 December 2009 for permanent settlement are exempt from passport renewal requirements if they lack Pakistan’s Computerized Nationality Identity Card (CNIC), provided they have not married or acquired immovable property in Pakistan and have no adverse police or security reports. PIOs: The exemption is also applicable to Persons of Indian Origin (PIO) who acquired Malaysian or Singaporean citizenship and returned to India on or before December 31, 2009, using passports issued by those countries, which have since expired and cannot be renewed. • However, they are required to obtain a visa category for their continued stay in India. Sri Lankan Tamil Refugees & Tibetans: Registered Sri Lankan Tamil refugees who took shelter in India on or before 9 January 2015, and eligible Tibetans who entered India with specified entry permits issued by the

Persecuted Religious Minorities: The revised rules have exempted members of Hindu, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi, and Christian communities from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, and Pakistan who entered India on or before December 31, 2024, after facing religious persecutions in these countries. • Additionally, the exemption is also applicable to those who entered without valid passports or other travel documents, as well as those whose documents have expired. However, in order to continue their stay in India, they need to obtain an appropriate visa after entering India. Other Key Provisions: Definition of Visa Manual: Through the amendment, the Government of India (GoI) defined “visa manual” document as a manual issued by the central government which contains instructions on visas; immigration; related matters; procedural incidental to immigration and visa administration. Cross-Border Travel: The revised rules allow citizens of India, Nepal and Bhutan to travel between these countries by land or air using identification documents prescribed in the government’s Visa Manual instead of passports. However, travel involving other countries, including transit through China, Macau, Hong Kong or Pakistan, requires valid passports and applicable visas, subject to prescribed conditions. About Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA): Union Minister- Amit Shah (Constituency- Gandhinagar, Gujarat) Minister of State (MoS)- Nityanand Rai (Constituency- Ujiarpur, Bihar); Bandi Sanjay Kumar (Constituency- Karimnagar, Telangana) Ministry of Minority Affairs Organises ‘Samavesh Se VIKAS’ in New Delhi, to Review PM VIKAS Implementation In November 2026, the Ministry of Minority Affairs (MoMA) organised ‘Samavesh Se VIKAS – Implementation Review and Stakeholder Dialogue’ at Samrasta Hall, Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi, Delhi, to review the implementation of Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) Scheme. New Framework Overview: New Framework: Effective from 1 April 2027, SEBI will allow Mutual Fund (MF) schemes to undertake net settlement of funds for outright transactions in the cash market. Settlement Mechanism: The SEBI stated that the facility would be offered at the individual mutual fund scheme level, while securities settlement would continue to follow the gross settlement mechanism. • There will be no adjustment of obligations between different schemes of the same mutual fund. Existing Framework: Under the current framework, institutional investors must settle cash market transactions on a gross basis, ensuring delivery of securities for every trade. • They are also prohibited from undertaking intraday squaring-off of transactions. Outright transaction: Outright transaction is defined as either a purchase or a sale transaction, but not both, in a particular security during the same settlement cycle. • If a mutual fund scheme buys and sells the same security within the same settlement cycle, those transactions will be classified as non-outright transactions and will not qualify for net settlement. Residual Obligation: If the value of outright purchase transactions exceeds the value of outright sale transactions, the scheme must fund the residual amount. • If outright sale proceeds exceed outright purchase obligations, the excess cannot be adjusted against non-outright purchase obligations and Non-outright purchase obligations will continue to be funded separately on a gross basis. Charges: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) and stamp duty will continue to apply on a delivery basis. Implementation and Compliance: • AMFI: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) will formulate implementation standards in consultation with stock exchanges, clearing corporations, custodians and other stakeholders. • Asset Management Companies (AMC) and Custodians: They must establish adequate systems and controls to identify eligible outright transactions and exclude non-outright transactions. • Audit Trail: Custodians must maintain records of gross obligations, netted fund obligations and excluded transactions. • Trustees: Trustees will review the implementation to ensure that the framework operates in the interest of mutual fund unit-holders Excluded Transactions: The following transactions will remain outside the scope of the net settlement framework: • Derivatives transactions. • Securities Lending and Borrowing (SLB) transactions. • Short-sale-related transactions. Revised Accredited Investor Framework: Manager Led Accreditation: Under the revised framework, AIFs (Alternate Investment Funds), SIFs (Specialised Investment Fund) and portfolio managers can also certify an investor’s eligibility directly. • This is an additional and optional route. The existing accreditation process through recognised Accreditation Agencies will continue.
